In this tutorial, we explore converting PyTorch models into TorchScript and ONNX formats, and subsequently serving them using FastAPI."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Model Serialization with TorchScript"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"TorchScript allows you to serialize your PyTorch model into a graph representation that can be executed independently of Python, such as in a C++ runtime."},{"order":5,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torchvision.models as models

# Initialize a pre-trained ResNet18 model
model = models.resnet18(pretrained=True)
model.eval()

# Create example input for tracing
example_input = torch.rand(1, 3, 224, 224)

# Trace the model
traced_script_module = torch.jit.trace(model, example_input)

# Save the serialized model
traced_script_module.save("model.pt")"},{"order":6,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Model Serialization with ONNX"},{"order":7,"type":"paragraph","text":"Open Neural Network Exchange (ONNX) is an open format built to represent machine learning models. It enables models to be trained in one framework and transferred to another for inference acceleration."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"import torch
import torchvision.models as models

model = models.resnet18(pretrained=True)
model.eval()

input_tensor = torch.randn(1, 3, 224, 224)

# Export to ONNX
torch.onnx.export(
    model,
    input_tensor,
    "model.onnx",
    export_params=True,
    opset_version=11,
    do_constant_folding=True,
    input_names=["input"],
    output_names=["output"],
    dynamic_axes={"input": {0: "batch_size"}, "output": {0: "batch_size"}}
)"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Building the Serving API with FastAPI"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"FastAPI is a modern, fast web framework for building APIs with Python. Below is an implementation of a scoring service using the ONNX runtime for efficient inference."},{"order":11,"type":"code","text":"from fastapi import FastAPI, File, UploadFile
import numpy as np
import onnxruntime as ort
from PIL import Image
import io

app = FastAPI(title="ONNX Model Server")

# Load ONNX session
ort_session = ort.InferenceSession("model.onnx")

def preprocess_image(image_bytes):
    image = Image.open(io.BytesIO(image_bytes)).convert("RGB")
    image = image.resize((224, 224))
    img_data = np.array(image).astype("float32") / 255.0
    img_data = np.transpose(img_data, (2, 0, 1))  # HWC to CHW
    img_data = np.expand_dims(img_data, axis=0)   # Add batch dimension
    return img_data

@app.post("/predict")
async def predict(file: UploadFile = File(...)):
    image_bytes = await file.read()
    input_data = preprocess_image(image_bytes)
    
    # Run inference
    input_name = ort_session.get_inputs()[0].name
    result = ort_session.run(None, {input_name: input_data})
    
    predicted_class = int(np.argmax(result[0]))
    return {"predicted_class": predicted_class}"},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Production Deployment"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always run model inference in non-blocking asynchronous endpoints or offload to background workers if handling heavy payloads."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use ONNX Runtime (ORT) or TensorRT for optimized execution speeds and reduced memory footprints compared to standard PyTorch interpreters."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Containerize your FastAPI application using Docker alongside appropriate ONNX Runtime GPU or CPU base images."}]
